security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel M-mode firmware (e.g. OpenSBI) or KVM host accesses menvcfg or menvcfgh CSR on a non-conformant hart that supports U-mode but does not implement these registers, or on an RV32 hart with S-mode that omits menvcfgh. Access to a non-existent CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception in M-mode/HS-mode, crashing the firmware or hypervisor before the kernel can handle it.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: csr_read\s+menvcfg|csr_write\s+menvcfg|csr_read\s+menvcfgh|csr_write\s+menvcfgh; SBI_EXT_SRST or SBI_EXT_DBENC paths that indirectly read/write menvcfg fields (CBZE, CBCFE, CBIE, STCE, PBMTE) without checking CSR existence
security_spec.summary: Spec mandates menvcfg must exist when U-mode is implemented and menvcfgh must exist when S-mode+XLEN=32; kernel/firmware accessing these CSRs on a non-conformant hart triggers illegal-instruction trap and system crash.

findings.finding: Under CONFIG_RISCV_M_MODE, CSR_ENVCFG resolves to CSR_MENVCFG (0x30a). If the M-mode kernel runs on a hart that lacks U-mode, menvcfg does not exist per spec (norm:menvcfg_menvcfgh_no_U_mode), and any csr_read/csr_write via CSR_ENVCFG would raise an illegal-instruction exception. The XLINUXENVCFG guard is a synthetic extension inferred from extensions with envcfg bits (ZICBOZ, ZICBOM, etc.), but these extensions don't strictly require U-mode — a Zicboz implementation for M-mode-only is theoretically possible. No runtime probe checks actual menvcfg CSR existence.
findings.snippet:
#ifdef CONFIG_RISCV_M_MODE
# define CSR_ENVCFG  CSR_MENVCFG
# define CSR_SCRATCH  CSR_MSCRATCH

spec_citations.excerpt: In harts with U-mode, menvcfg must be implemented, but all WARL fields may be read-only zero. For harts with S-mode and XLEN=32, menvcfgh must be similarly implemented. If U-mode is not supported, then registers menvcfg and menvcfgh do not exist.

findings.finding: Context-switch path correctly uses ALTERNATIVE with RISCV_ISA_EXT_XLINUXENVCFG guard, patching to nop if the envcfg CSR is absent. Under normal S-mode, CSR_ENVCFG resolves to CSR_SENVCFG (0x10a), not CSR_MENVCFG (0x30a). The senvcfg is saved/restored per-task via thread.envcfg. This correctly avoids any direct menvcfg access.

Suspend path saves envcfg only when XLINUXENVCFG extension is present. Under normal S-mode, this operates on senvcfg (CSR 0x10a), not menvcfg. The restore path at line 47 similarly guards with the same check. No direct menvcfg access.

Shadow-stack and landing-pad enable/disable paths write SSE and LPE bits via csr_write(CSR_ENVCFG). In normal S-mode this resolves to senvcfg. The menvcfg.SSE bit is managed by M-mode firmware via the earlier SBI FWFT call in head.S. The kernel correctly operates only on the S-mode-visible alias. Writes to senvcfg.SSE when menvcfg.SSE=0 would be ignored (bit is read-only zero per spec), which is safe.

spec_citations.excerpt: When menvcfg.SSE is 0, the henvcfg.SSE and senvcfg.SSE fields are read-only zero.

findings.finding: WARL probing of PMM field uses csr_set/csr_read_clear on CSR_ENVCFG (senvcfg under S-mode). The menvcfg.PMM bits control pointer masking in M-mode; the kernel probes senvcfg.PMM (the S-mode alias) to determine supported PMLEN values. tagged_addr_init() first checks RISCV_ISA_EXT_SUPM before probing. No direct menvcfg access.

XLINUXENVCFG pseudo-extension correctly models that envcfg CSR existence is implied by extensions defining envcfg bits (ZICBOM, ZICBOZ, ZICFILP, ZICFISS, SMNPM, SSNPM all declare XLINUXENVCFG as a superset). This provides the guard used by all csr_read/csr_write paths to avoid accessing non-existent CSRs. The design is sound: if no extension uses envcfg bits, the CSR is never touched.

spec_citations.excerpt: In harts with U-mode, menvcfg must be implemented, but all WARL fields may be read-only zero.

findings.finding: Startup code sets CBZE and CBCFE bits in current->thread.envcfg, which are later written to the hardware CSR via __switch_to_envcfg(). The guards check RISCV_ISA_EXT_ZICBOZ and RISCV_ISA_EXT_ZICBOM, which imply XLINUXENVCFG. The actual CSR write happens only after the ALTERNATIVE check passes. No direct menvcfg access.

Boot path issues SBI_EXT_FWFT_SET for SHADOW_STACK to tell M-mode firmware (OpenSBI) to set menvcfg.SSE. The kernel does NOT write menvcfg itself — it delegates to firmware via the SBI ecall. The return value is checked (beqz a0, 1f) and gracefully degrades by setting the riscv_nousercfi flag. This is the correct architecture: firmware owns menvcfg, kernel uses the SBI abstraction.
findings.snippet:
li a7, SBI_EXT_FWFT
li a6, SBI_EXT_FWFT_SET
li a0, SBI_FWFT_SHADOW_STACK
li a1, 1
li a2, SBI_FWFT_SET_FLAG_LOCK
ecall
beqz a0, 1f

findings.finding: Secondary hart boot path mirrors the primary hart's SBI FWFT call, including the same error-path handling. SMP hotplug is correctly handled: each hart independently requests firmware to enable shadow stack access. No direct menvcfg access.
findings.snippet:
li a7, SBI_EXT_FWFT
li a6, SBI_EXT_FWFT_SET
li a0, SBI_FWFT_SHADOW_STACK
li a1, 1
li a2, SBI_FWFT_SET_FLAG_LOCK
ecall
beqz a0, 1f

findings.finding: KVM config setup sets henvcfg bits (PBMTE, STCE, CBIE, CBCFE, CBZE, ADUE), NOT menvcfg. Under HS-mode (the hypervisor extension), henvcfg (CSR 0x60a) is the HS-mode-local envcfg. If menvcfg has a corresponding bit set to 0, the henvcfg bit is read-only zero per spec and the write is silently ignored — no crash risk. The SMSTATEEN0_HSENVCFG bit is correctly set to grant HS-mode access to the henvcfg CSR. No direct menvcfg access.

spec_citations.excerpt: When menvcfg.PBMTE is zero, henvcfg.PBMTE is read-only zero.

findings.finding: VCPU load writes henvcfg to hardware via nacl_csr_write(CSR_HENVCFG) or csr_write(CSR_HENVCFG). On RV32, henvcfgh is also written (CSR_HENVCFGH). This is correct: henvcfg and henvcfgh always exist when the H extension is implemented. The NACL shared-memory CSR path (lines 596-598) correctly includes henvcfg in the batch-sync CSR set. No menvcfg/menvcfgh access.

SVADU enablement check correctly notes: 'henvcfg.ADUE is read-only zero if menvcfg.ADUE is zero'. Uses arch_has_hw_pte_young() as the runtime gate, which checks whether the kernel itself has ADUE enabled (implying menvcfg.ADUE=1 was set by firmware). This correctly prevents offering Svadu to guests when the host doesn't have menvcfg.ADUE=1. No direct menvcfg access.

spec_citations.excerpt: When menvcfg.ADUE is zero, henvcfg.ADUE is read-only zero.

findings.finding: KVM SBI FWFT pointer-masking PMLEN uses CSR_HENVCFG (henvcfg.PMM), not menvcfg.PMM. The code is CONFIG_32BIT-guarded (lines 130-148), correctly reflecting that menvcfg.PMM is read-only zero on RV32 (PMM is only meaningful at XLEN=64). The host kernel writes henvcfg.PMM to set VS-mode pointer masking. No direct menvcfg access.

spec_citations.excerpt: PMM field in menvcfg controls pointer masking for S/HS-mode or U-mode. PMM field is read-only zero on RV32. When Smnpm is not implemented, PMM is read-only zero.

findings.finding: KVM SRST handler is a pure system-reset SBI call translator (shutdown, cold/warm reboot forwarded as KVM_SYSTEM_EVENT). It does NOT read or write any envcfg/menvcfg fields (CBZE, CBCFE, CBIE, STCE, PBMTE). The spec concern about SBI_EXT_SRST indirectly accessing menvcfg fields is not applicable to this code path — SRST has no envcfg interaction in the kernel implementation.

    ...
    case SBI_EXT_SRST_RESET:

findings.finding: Host-side SRST is a pure SBI ecall for system reset. No envcfg/menvcfg CSR access. The SBI ecall is handled by M-mode firmware (OpenSBI), which performs the actual system reset. The kernel does not touch menvcfg in this path.

CSR numbers defined as 0x30a (menvcfg) and 0x31a (menvcfgh). These are correct per the RISC-V privileged spec. Only referenced via CSR_ENVCFG aliasing under CONFIG_RISCV_M_MODE (line 491). Under normal S-mode configuration, CSR_ENVCFG resolves to CSR_SENVCFG (0x10a, line 516), so these M-mode CSR definitions are never used.

spec_citations.excerpt: menvcfg CSR address 0x30A, MRW (Machine Read/Write); menvcfgh CSR address 0x31A, MRW

findings.finding: envcfg_update_bits updates task->thread.envcfg and writes to current CSR if task==current. Under S-mode, writes to senvcfg, not menvcfg. The task==current guard ensures only the running task's CSR is touched, avoiding races on remote tasks. Called from flush_thread and prctl PMLEN setter. No menvcfg involvement.
